main_body: Barn: a large red tile roof slope (rows 5-57) with a dormer and chimney, above a red plank wall with a double X-braced door, two windows and a stone base
top_band: Roof slope: cream ridge highlight row 6 and orange row 7, then tile rows (L 42-110) down to a cream eave line at rows 56-57. The ridge and slope read as a horizontal surface seen from above.
evidence: The roof is drawn as a large visible slope with a lighter cream ridge and eave line. A dark shadow row sits under the eave, then the vertical wall with its own shading. The door and windows have dark inset frames, and the dormer has its own small roof slope, so the roof and wall both satisfy the 3/4 contract. This matches how the Beodeul house references draw roof over wall.

style.evidence: The roof tiles have a good scalloped rhythm with highlight, mid and dark steps. The rest is thin. Walls are simple vertical stripes of 2-3 tones, and the door and window frames are flat light grey with line braces. The stone base is only a few greys. Distinct colours (23) are far below both references (66 and 185), and median colours per tile (7) are below 11 and 18. The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral), which is acceptable. There are no flat-fill blocks by the measure. Overall the piece looks flatter and thinner than the references, so it fails.
